# 1.2.74 - a room is what a GM marked, and the Class Trial has a hall of its own

The twenty-first and twenty-second stages on the way to 1.3.0 (E12 and E13),
released together: a room is what a GM marked, every rule is handed the scene it
judges, and the Class Trial has a hall of its own. Most of it was measured in
the headless harness, some only read in the code, none tried at a table.

## Before installing

1. **Isometric Perspective and LiveKit (`avclient-livekit`) are now required,**
   as Dice So Nice is: installed and switched on. Without one the module stops
   at load: the GM gets a window naming each as "not installed" or "installed,
   but switched off" and a player a notice that stays on screen. No LiveKit
   server is asked whether it answers. The recommended-modules window and its
   setting `recommendsSilenced` are gone. Not tried at a table (LIVE-E13-11).
2. **Back up the world, and the case, and note the version you ran,** so a
   problem can be traced back. **On The Forge, install from this release's
   manifest URL;** whether v14 and The Forge offer the two modules is not
   measured (LIVE-E13-11).
3. **The first load marks the rooms the world already had,** once: from 1.2.74 a
   region is a room only when a GM ticked "This is a room" in Room Setup's Doors
   tab, so on the primary GM's browser every named region with no behaviours,
   not drawn by a player and not yet decided is marked, and the primary GM is
   whispered one report, "Rooms marked", of what was marked and what was left
   and why. Season setup's row "Every named region is decided: a room or not"
   names those still waiting (on a real world's copy: LIVE-E12-08).
4. **Texts and settings.** Room Setup's Doors column "Not a room" is now "No
   privacy" and gains "This is a room" and "Neighbours" columns and a Scenes
   tab. Nothing new in the settings window: three hidden settings are added
   (`sceneRoles`, `playerRegions`, `gmTrialCast`) and `recommendsSilenced`
   removed (122 settings registered in settings.mjs, 120 at 1.2.73).
   `lang/en.json` goes from 3214 to 3316 strings, `lang/pl.json` from 3961 to
   4083. The handbooks and README were updated.
5. **A macro may need changing.** `placeRemnant` and `applySceneVisionMode`
   given no scene do nothing and say so; `setStash`, `setVaultRoom` and
   `setRestRoom` given none take the first scene with that room; `createProject`
   refuses a room no scene holds; `setClock` refuses to begin an Eclipse in a
   Class Trial. A 1.2.73 browser beside a 1.2.74 GM was not tried.

## At the table

### Rooms, floors and Room Setup

- **A room is what a GM marked.** A region with a Teleport or level-change
  behaviour, or one a player drew, is never a room. A player's change to the
  mark is put back and the GMs told (with no record of the mark from before the
  change, nothing is put back and the GMs are told to check the region).
  **Several regions with one name are one room:** a lock, a seal or a Neighbours
  list on any piece holds for all, Room Setup shows one row and writes every
  piece, and the fog outlines it whole (what a player's canvas draws:
  LIVE-E12-09). Neighbours: blank, the walls decide (a corner is not enough);
  with a list, exactly those, and either room's list counts.
- **Floors (Foundry v14 Levels).** A room is read on the token's own floor; a
  change of floor is a move, refused, charged and sent back like a step. Stairs
  cost one crossing like a door, a floor change inside one room is free, and
  where the scene has stairs a change between rooms they do not link is refused.
  The fog works one floor at a time and **Floors** buttons offer a player their
  own floor and the floors holding a room they found. With token vision off a
  player sees only the door controls of rooms the fog leaves clear or veiled.
  Measured on the harness's model of Levels, not v14 (LIVE-E12-02, -03, -05).
- **A student placed past the rules** (a token a player's console put in a room
  the rules refuse) is no witness to a body and no third party to a murder until
  they stand somewhere they could have walked to, and the GMs are whispered. The
  record is the primary GM's: a GM who becomes primary afterwards may read them
  as lawful until they move (scenario 66, P2).
- **A GM's rename carries what named the old room** once the room's last piece
  of the old name on that scene has the new one - keys, stashed items, notes of
  a stash found, discovery, a project's, plant's and assembly's room, the
  Mastermind's room, Neighbours lists, a Despair Call's seal, the bodies found
  there - and the GMs are whispered what moved; keys, stashed items and the
  Mastermind's room move only where they cannot mean a room of the old name on
  another scene. A rename onto an existing room joins it and carries nothing; a
  player's rename carries nothing.
- **Room Setup writes to the scene it was opened on,** whatever scene is on
  screen at Apply, and says how many rooms it changed (its look: LIVE-E12-06).
  Its **Scenes** tab (the last) links the **School** and the **Trial hall** (two
  different scenes), shows the hall's cast and holds **Prepare the hall**, and
  names a hall with regions marked as rooms, a student a player plays with no
  token there, a second token for one character and an unlinked token. A GM
  keeps Foundry's Scenes tab, scene navigation and macro hotbar in both themes,
  and when the module stops for a missing required module; a player has none
  (read in the stylesheet; whether Foundry loads it then, and Stained Glass:
  LIVE-E13-11, -09).

### The Class Trial, its hall and its voice

- **Every road into the trial takes the table to the hall** (Start the Class
  Trial, Edit campaign, the phase select, `setPhase`, `setClock`): the hall is
  activated, so Foundry moves every connected browser. **Every road out hides
  the cast and takes the table back** (End the trial, the chapter end, the same
  selects and calls, the season reset): to the room chosen in End the trial,
  else the school, else the scene active when the trial opened, else the table
  stays in the hall and the GMs are told (the last case read in the code). With
  no hall linked the trial opens where the table is, as before. Measured on the
  harness's four browsers (not at a table; a late browser: LIVE-E13-01, -02).
- **Start the Class Trial** names the hall and how many tokens it will show, or
  says that no hall is linked and the table stays where it is. Entering the
  trial whispers the GMs, by name, the students a player plays who have no token
  in the hall (a tier-2 test). Inside a trial the console's **Show the hall**
  and **Back to school** move the table and keep the phase. The hall is a place
  for nobody: no rooms, fog, discovery, movement limit or trail there, and a
  token in it is never where its student is.
- **With a hall linked, End the trial asks for a room:** every room of every
  scene with rooms, the school's first, or Cancel; the verdict does not end the
  trial. The table goes to that scene, the hall's tokens are hidden, the living
  go to random points in the room as after a body, Monocubs too, the dead and
  Monokuma stay. The chapter-end screen's End the trial moves nobody.
- **A living student on another place scene comes too, as a copy under a new
  id** (data, hidden state, place in a combat); with tokens on two such scenes
  the one the module reads as where they stand moves, and the GMs are told the
  other stays. The copy stays only when the old token is gone: if the create is
  refused, or the delete is and the copy can be taken back, the move is undone
  and the student is named; if not even that works, the student stands on both
  scenes and is named. A carry cut short by the GM's browser closing leaves a
  copy marked with its source, named at the next GM's load (measured by calling
  the load step). Headless, with a stand-in for a Combat, the copy equals the
  old token field by field (id, position and floor aside; tier-2 "End the trial
  carries a student's token across scenes whole"); what v14 keeps is unknown
  (LIVE-E13-10).
- **A student who cannot be moved stays and is named:** "{n} living student
  could not be moved and stays where they stood: {names}. Move them by hand."
  (no room on their scene, only in the hall, a create or delete refused).
- **The trial is one voice room** for the living, the dead, Monocubs, the GMs
  and an account with no character, hall linked or not. **The dead listen and do
  not speak** is the table's rule, stated beside Start the Class Trial; the
  module mutes nobody. LiveKit itself was not tried (LIVE-E13-05).
- **The GMs choose, and only that cast is shown.** Until a tick changes,
  Monokuma and each student a player owns are shown (the dead too, immovable for
  their player - refused on the school and in the hall, scenario 41 phase n -
  under the dead overlay, LIVE-E13-04; and Monocubs); a student nobody plays and
  a second token for one character are hidden. Only `hidden` is written; the
  choice is kept in the GMs' browsers for the season and read again at each GM's
  load and on every change of the hall's link (a player's change made while no
  GM was connected is taken as the hall's state at the next GM's load). A
  player's change to a hall token's `hidden` is put back and a token a player
  deletes there stays gone, both told to the GMs (whether v14 lets a player do
  either: LIVE-E13-08). If the choice has not reached the browser that opens the
  trial, nobody is shown and the GMs are told.
- **A dark hall is named.** With token vision on, global light off or
  exploration fog on in the linked hall, the tab says so and entering the trial
  whispers the GMs to tick "Prepare the hall" in Room Setup's Scenes tab and
  press Apply; Prepare is off until ticked. A hall whose rooms were drawn before
  it was linked is already lit by the room fog (on the primary GM's browser,
  with the room fog on) and is not named; switching the room fog off puts its
  old vision back (read in the code, not run).
- **An Eclipse cannot start during a Class Trial** (the owner's decision DZ1):
  the API, the GM panel, the HUD and the clock refuse (the panel's refusal read
  in the code). The HUD draws no chevron in a trial; the others warn that no
  Eclipse was started and to end the trial first.

### Tier 0 items, and the GM's screen

- **A Tier 0 tool or weapon breaks on any roll it is used in,** Hope, Despair or
  critical; Tiers 1 to 3 lose a point only on a Despair (the Tool and the knife
  swing are driven, the other roads that wear an item read in the code). The
  sheet says "Single use". An item with no tier counts as Tier 0.
- **Rules are not decided from the GM's screen** (no GM-side rule depends on the
  scene or floor the GM is looking at). Who stands in a room, the lights'
  verdict on a murder, a theft, a trap, Listen, Rest and Move the body read the
  scene the token stands on; a project is reached only in its room on its own
  scene. 30 rows of `CAMERA_READERS` still read the screen, for drawing, windows
  and diagnostics.

## Changed

- The new leaves `rooms.mjs` and `trial-scene.mjs`, `carryAcross` in
  `call-world.mjs` and the clause `markRooms` (since 1.2.74) in `migrate.mjs`;
  the GM bridge's project guards ask the project's own scene and a send-back is
  judged on the floor; `relay-guard.mjs` changed one comment. The manifest's
  Foundry and Daggerheart versions are unchanged.
- **New tests:** 34 numbered ones (17 in tier 0, 17 in tier 1: R113 to R120,
  R379 to R387, R410, R411, R430 to R442, R470, R471), 70 tier-2 tests, and
  scenarios 66-rooms and 41-trial-scene in the ci set (23, 21 at 1.2.73). Next
  free: R472. One scene put into room-based vision now gets the singular
  message, "Room-based visibility switched on for {count} scene." (R471 reads
  every `plural()` call for the field it counts on). Scenario 41 now records
  that a hall drawn before it was linked is already lit, and models a hall
  nobody prepared.

## Known gaps

- Twenty live checks stand open, items 163 to 182 of the audit's section 9.2
  (LIVE-E12-01 to 09, LIVE-E13-01 to 11): v14's floors, fog, door controls and
  Room Setup on a real canvas, what v14 keeps of a moved token's copy, a late
  browser, the hall's overlay, dice and LiveKit, navigation and hotbar in both
  themes, and `requires`. Not in that list: the width of the "Single use" label
  in the sheet row.
- The witnesses of an action roll (briefing, project work, sabotage, clean-up)
  are counted on the roller's browser, where the primary's record is not held. A
  player's rename, or one written with `noHook`, is not judged for a split; a
  stair is read at its centre only; a Neighbours name with a comma cannot be
  listed. The clock setting written directly with `game.settings.set` passes no
  check.
- Read in the code, not run: the browser side of the trial's voice plan; the
  speaker readers an old token id strands (the system's own not read); the GM
  chrome's three render hooks (names from memory); whether a move in the hall
  triggers an Eclipse rule; whether a GM's move announces a body in the room End
  the trial chooses.
- Not measured: two GMs carrying the same student at once; a token delete that
  never answers holds End the trial, and the GMs hear of it only at the next
  GM's load; whether v14 lets a player delete their own token by default.
- The tier-2 suite at a table empties the world's scene links for its run and
  puts them back at its end; a run cut off half way leaves them empty: link them
  again in the Scenes tab.
